summary: Two-story live-in tower in Stillwater State Forest north of Whitefish, MT, built after a 1911 log lookout; staffed in fire season and rented in summer.

facts.design: Two-story concrete and frame live-in tower with a 15 by 15 ft cab; the 1941 L-4 cab was moved to a museum in 1987

access.note: Rented by reservation through the Montana DNRC in July and September; August is kept for fire staffing and is not rentable.

visit.trail_note: Reached by vehicle on a narrow, bumpy road; the Flathead Beacon describes 12 miles of it from Olney. The Ralph Thayer Memorial Trail runs next to the lookout. Visitors bring their own water.

events.note: First log cabin, about a mile east of the summit.
Another log cabin, a D-1 log cupola cabin, added on the summit.
A 10-foot pole L-4 tower was constructed by 1941.
Allen Overton listed as a lookout.
Wendy Boggess listed as a lookout, 1975 to 1977.
Present two-story concrete and frame tower replaced the pole tower. A 2010 newspaper dates completion of the existing 15-by-15-foot structure to 1984.
The L-4 cab was moved to a museum 1 mile south of Kalispell.
Lightning-ignited 860-acre fire east of the peak, contained within two weeks.
Stillwater State Forest offered the lookout for rent as a pilot project at $35 a night.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 9, 2021.
Volunteer crew replaced decking and repainted the structure over a weekend.

corrections.proposed: Two-story concrete and frame live-in tower built 1983; the L-4 was the 1941 pole-tower cab, moved to a museum in 1987
corrections.why: The register entry says the L-4 cab sat on the 1941 pole tower and was moved to a museum in 1987. The current building is the 1983 two-story tower.

corrections.proposed: omit (no source read gives a height)
corrections.why: None of the sources read gives a height for the tower, and 3.0 m does not fit a two-story live-in tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Flathead Beacon (2007), the register and the Whitefish Pilot (2021) date the present tower to 1983. The Daily Inter Lake (2010) says the existing 15-by-15-foot structure was completed in 1984. The story uses 1983 and notes the 1984 date.
Visit Montana says about 23 miles north of Whitefish, the Daily Inter Lake says about 24 miles north, and the Flathead Beacon describes 12 miles of road from Olney. The story gives no single figure.

sources.title: Restoration project on Werner Peak Lookout preserves legacy

notes_for_editor: Built and status are well supported. The 1983 versus 1984 date for the present tower is a real conflict and is noted in the story. Staffing (August and emergencies) and the 2026 rental terms come from the Visit Montana listing and the firelookout.com profile; recheck the price and dates before publishing. A Montana Standard search lead about a Werner Peak fire complex threatening the lookout was not opened and its date is unclear, so it is left out. The brief's elevation_m 2119.9 is a little off from the 6,960 ft (about 2,121 m) the sources give; not changed.
